title: Case: e-commerce CDC into an Iceberg lakehouse read by Snowflake
summary: An end-to-end design from Postgres CDC through Kafka, Flink and Spark into Iceberg bronze, silver and gold, read by Snowflake and served through a semantic model.

blocks.text: 47.1 Context and requirements

An online retailer runs on Postgres (`orders`, `order_items`, `customers`, `payments`): 40 million orders, 300k changes a day, 10x spikes on sale days. Nightly dumps are a day old and miss hard deletes, so the warehouse drifts. Analysts use Snowflake; data scientists want Spark on the same data, and nobody wants heavy reads on the primary.

head: Option
Strengths
Weaknesses
rows: A. Cloud ELT into Snowflake tables (chapter 41)
Spark users export or pay Snowflake compute; history locked in one engine
B. Iceberg lakehouse, Snowflake reads via catalog (chapter 42)
one open copy, any engine, replay from bronze
more to operate; table maintenance is the team's job
stateful multi-table joins are costly and hard to correct; 15 min does not need it

blocks.title: Architecture decision record
blocks.text:
ADR-012  CDC lakehouse for commerce analytics       Status: accepted
Decision: B. Debezium (pgoutput) -> Kafka -> Flink appends Iceberg bronze
  (commit per 2-min checkpoint) -> Spark MERGE silver every 10 min ->
  dbt-on-Spark gold star -> Snowflake reads gold via catalog integration.
Why not A: duplicate storage, lock-in. Why not C: unneeded latency cost.
Consequences: platform team owns compaction and snapshot expiry; Spark is
  the only writer; Snowflake is read-only on these tables.
Revisit if: freshness target drops below 1 minute.
*Revisit if* turns a decision into a testable hypothesis; interviewers probe exactly that.

blocks.text: 47.4 Data model and layers

**Bronze**: one row per Debezium event with key, `op` (`c`, `u`, `d`, `r` for snapshot reads), flattened `after` columns, source LSN, `ts_ms` and `ingested_at`. Append-only, partitioned by `days(ingested_at)`, so any later layer can be rebuilt by replay (chapter 13).

**Silver**: current state, one row per key, with `_lsn`; money as `DECIMAL(18,2)`, timestamps UTC (chapter 14). Partition by stable business time (`months(created_at)`), not update time, or every update of an old order lands in a new partition.

**Gold**: a Kimball star (chapter 8): `fct_orders` (one row per order), `fct_order_items`, `dim_customer` as SCD2 (chapter 9), `dim_product`, `dim_date`. `fct_orders.customer_order_seq` ranks the order in the customer's history, so repeat rate becomes a cheap filter.
47.5 Pipelines with code

Debezium reads a slot with the `pgoutput` plugin (`topic.prefix=shop`, `snapshot.mode=initial`, heartbeats on). Delete events carry only the key unless `REPLICA IDENTITY FULL` is set; the key is enough here.

blocks.title: Flink SQL
blocks.text:
CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE orders_src (
  `before` ROW<id BIGINT>,
  `after`  ROW<id BIGINT, customer_id BIGINT, status STRING,
               total_amount STRING, created_at BIGINT>,
  op STRING, ts_ms BIGINT, `source` ROW<lsn BIGINT>
) WITH (
  'connector' = 'kafka', 'topic' = 'shop.public.orders',
  'properties.bootstrap.servers' = 'kafka:9092',
  'properties.group.id' = 'bronze-orders', 'format' = 'json');

SET 'execution.checkpointing.interval' = '2 min';

INSERT INTO lake.bronze.orders_cdc   -- lake = Iceberg REST catalog
SELECT COALESCE(`after`.id, `before`.id), op, `after`.customer_id,
       `after`.status, CAST(`after`.total_amount AS DECIMAL(18,2)),
       `after`.created_at, `source`.lsn, ts_ms, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
FROM orders_src WHERE op IS NOT NULL;  -- skip tombstones
The Iceberg Flink sink commits per checkpoint, so the interval sets freshness and file count: 2 minutes is 720 commits per table per day. Check Debezium's type encodings before casting.

blocks.title: Spark SQL: silver MERGE with deletes
blocks.text:
MERGE INTO lake.silver.orders t
USING (SELECT * FROM (
         SELECT b.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY lsn DESC) rn
         FROM lake.bronze.orders_cdc b
         WHERE ingested_at > '${watermark}') WHERE rn = 1) s
ON t.order_id = s.order_id
WHEN MATCHED AND s.op = 'd' AND s.lsn > t._lsn THEN DELETE
WHEN MATCHED AND s.lsn > t._lsn THEN UPDATE SET
  t.status = s.status, t.total_amount = s.total_amount, t._lsn = s.lsn
WHEN NOT MATCHED AND s.op <> 'd' THEN INSERT
  (order_id, customer_id, status, total_amount, created_at, _lsn)
  VALUES (s.order_id, s.customer_id, s.status, s.total_amount,
          timestamp_millis(s.created_at), s.lsn);

Three rules: keep the latest event per key, never let an older LSN overwrite newer state, never insert a key whose last event is a delete. The orchestrator keeps the watermark with some overlap (chapter 30); the LSN guard makes overlap harmless.

blocks.title: dbt (dbt-spark): models/gold/fct_orders.sql

blocks.text: `customer_order_seq` is a window over a customer's whole history, so the increment must recompute *all* orders of every touched customer, not just changed rows.

blocks.title: Snowflake SQL: externally managed Iceberg table
blocks.text:
CREATE CATALOG INTEGRATION glue_lake
  CATALOG_SOURCE = GLUE  CATALOG_NAMESPACE = 'gold'  TABLE_FORMAT = ICEBERG
  GLUE_AWS_ROLE_ARN = 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/sf-glue'
  GLUE_CATALOG_ID = '123456789012'  GLUE_REGION = 'eu-west-1'
  ENABLED = TRUE;

CREATE ICEBERG TABLE analytics.gold.fct_orders
  EXTERNAL_VOLUME = 'lake_s3'  CATALOG = 'glue_lake'
  CATALOG_TABLE_NAME = 'fct_orders'  AUTO_REFRESH = TRUE;
A REST catalog uses `CATALOG_SOURCE = ICEBERG_REST`; refresh options differ per catalog type, so check the current documentation (chapter 28).

47.6 Operations, cost and failure modes

blocks.title: Spark SQL maintenance, scheduled by the orchestrator

blocks.text: Compact bronze hourly into 256-512 MB files. Each merge-on-read MERGE adds delete files that slow reads until rewritten (chapter 25). Expire snapshots by policy (7 days here), then remove orphans with a generous `older_than`.

head: Signal
Alert when
rows: Kafka lag of the bronze job
Daily row count Postgres vs silver

blocks.text: **Cost**: the always-on Kafka/Connect cluster is usually the largest fixed cost; Flink is one small 24/7 job; Spark runs a few ephemeral hours a day; Snowflake bills only BI warehouse time, more for poorly compacted tables.

items: **Slot bloat**: Debezium stops and the slot pins WAL until the primary disk fills. Monitor slot lag; keep a drop-and-resnapshot runbook.
**Schema drift**: a new Postgres column is ignored by a fixed Flink DDL. Use Avro with a schema registry or alert on unknown fields.
**Re-snapshot**: replayed `r` events flip silver to old values without the LSN guard.
**Commit conflicts**: compaction and MERGE commit to the same table; one retries or fails. Compact partitions the MERGE is not touching.
**Stale reader**: Snowflake refresh lags and dashboards disagree with Spark. Compare the snapshot id Snowflake sees with the catalog.

blocks.title: Sale-day spike
blocks.text: Changes jump tenfold; Flink writes many more small files and the 10-minute MERGE takes 14.
items: The orchestrator allows one MERGE per table at a time, so batches grow instead of overlapping.
Bronze compaction moves from hourly to every 15 minutes for the day.
The team accepts a one-day freshness breach instead of permanently scaling Spark.

blocks.title: Add payments and refunds
blocks.text: Finance wants revenue net of partial refunds by refund date and cash collected by payment date, at the same freshness. Payments change status several times and are sometimes deleted by a back-office tool. Extend bronze, silver, gold and the semantic model.
hints: What is the grain of a payments fact: payment, status change, or money movement?
Which date does each metric aggregate on?
What happens to 2024 revenue when a refund for a 2024 order arrives today?

items: Log-based CDC on a Postgres slot captures updates and deletes without loading the primary.
Bronze is an append-only change log; silver is current state via MERGE, per-key dedup and LSN guards.
Flink's Iceberg sink commits per checkpoint: the interval sets freshness and small-file pressure.
Snowflake reads externally managed Iceberg through a catalog integration; one engine writes.
Compaction, delete-file rewrites, expiry and orphan removal are scheduled, monitored operations.
Ratio metrics (AOV, repeat rate) aggregate numerator and denominator before dividing.

blocks.q: Why does the silver MERGE check `s.lsn > t._lsn`?
options: To skip rows from the initial snapshot
So replayed or reordered events never overwrite newer state
Snowflake requires an LSN column on Iceberg tables
To force merge-on-read instead of copy-on-write
blocks.explain: The LSN orders source changes, making the MERGE idempotent under replay. Snapshot rows are applied, not skipped, when newer.

blocks.q: The bronze Flink job checkpoints every 30 seconds. Most likely side effect?
options: Many small files and snapshots to maintain
blocks.explain: Each checkpoint is an Iceberg commit with new files. Bronze is append-only, so deletes are not at stake.

blocks.q: Postgres disk grows overnight while traffic is normal. Check first?
options: Replication slot lag: a stopped Debezium makes the slot retain WAL
blocks.explain: A logical slot keeps WAL until the consumer confirms it; the others are not on the Postgres disk.

blocks.q: Why is a ratio metric for AOV better than averaging daily AOV over a month?
options: It sums revenue and orders first, so busy days weigh correctly
blocks.explain: Averaging daily ratios weighs a quiet day like a sale day. Nothing is precomputed.
